reading.body:
Expedient Owings Mills in Owings Mills, Maryland, publishes 2.3 MW of IT capacity across 22,000 square feet of technical space, operated by Expedient.

At 10 kW per rack, a common enterprise colocation density, that load supports roughly 230 racks. At 40 kW per rack, a density closer to AI training workloads, it supports roughly 58 racks. The operator has not published a per-rack power envelope, so neither figure is the operator's own claim, only what the published megawattage implies under each assumption.

Expedient Owings Mills holds 3 published certifications: PCI DSS (the standard required to handle payment card data), HIPAA (handling of protected health information), HITRUST (a healthcare-focused security framework built on top of HIPAA). Together these qualify the facility for regulated workloads spanning security auditing, payments, and healthcare data, though which specific tenants rely on which certification is not disclosed.

Maryland has 2 facilities mapped in this site's dataset, of which 2 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 4.6 MW. Expedient Owings Mills contributes 2.3 MW of that total. At that published size it is a small facility relative to what frontier AI training infrastructure requires, which now runs into the tens or hundreds of megawatts, though it may still support inference workloads or smaller-scale AI applications.
